# RIP authoring

A RIP is written in one of two formats. If product/ contains `.ready` files,
follow **.ready records** below; otherwise follow **Markdown and Mermaid**.

At the start of a work session, check pending Ready Room messages with
`read_messages`, and take a message with `acknowledge_message` before acting on
it; if it was already taken, leave it. When a `rip_change` message names a
revision, read it with `read_rip`. Its page 0 is an index: every file's status
against the repository RIP at base_commit (added, changed, or unchanged), size,
and page, the removed paths, and for a `.ready` RIP the record-change counts.
Read the pages you need with `read_rip` and `page`: record changes (the added,
removed, and changed records with their display ids and changed fields) come
first, then file contents in path order, and a long file continues on the next
page. Bring the change into product/ directly or in your own way. Ask Ready
Room with `ask_product` when intent is unclear; its answers interpret the RIP
and do not extend it. If Ready Room is unavailable, continue from the
repository RIP.

## .ready records

This is a format guide, not product behavior or authorization to change intent.
Read product/product.ready and the records of the modules you touch first.

This RIP is a graph of typed records. Each record is ONE YAML file ending in
.ready under product/: one record, one file, one fact. Records refer to each
other by id; diagrams, outlines and exports are derived, never stored. Folders
are a convention (product/<module>/journeys/, sequences/, rules/, data/, ...);
the loader reads every .ready file under product/. Describe the current
intended end state in present tense, never a patch plan or history.

Every record has: ready: 1, kind, id, and optionally display_id, aliases,
rationale, notes, files, tags.

- id: lowercase dotted machine id (shops.claim.enter-email). Never change or
  reuse one; other records link to it. A new record needs a new unique id.
- display_id: stable human id (FLOW-012, SEQ-014a, DATA-ACCOUNT, RULE-ACCESS)
  that people and code comments cite. Unique across the RIP.
- aliases: retired ids and old anchors that still resolve to this record.
- rationale (why it is shaped this way) and notes are the only Markdown fields.
- files: [{path, title?, role?}] supplementary product/ files (contracts,
  prompts, SVG mockups). Never logic and never copied code.
- tags: [{tag, text}] for annotations with no dedicated field.

Main kinds and their main fields (a field the format does not define is
refused):

- product (name, outcome, boundary, exclusions, measures, dcl), module (name,
  summary, owns, invariants, runs_in), actor, capability (outcome, actors,
  owners), system (role, system_kind, connections, units, secrets: names only).
- journey (module, actors, title, summary, steps in order, sequences, entries,
  related) and step (journey, title, step_kind screen|action|system|decision|
  outcome|error, surface, presentation, copy {title, body[], actions[],
  hints[]} quoted verbatim, sees, does, next [{to|$return, label, when}],
  sequences, rules, data). surface (module, name, surface_kind, route, parent).
- operation (module, name, summary, params, returns, errors [{code, status,
  when, copy}], http, auth, sequence).
- sequence (module, title, trigger {trigger_kind, text}, operation,
  participants, items). rule (module, title, then one or more of when/then/
  otherwise, decision {nodes, edges}, table, judge, rules; plus default,
  constraints, params). constant (module, name, value, unit, source).
- entity (module, table, name, summary, columns [{name, type, keys, fk,
  nullable, default, check, values}], primary_key, indexes [{id badge, name,
  unique, columns, purpose}], relationships [{to, label, link fk|logical,
  from_card, to_card}], access, lifecycle), entity_group (entities),
  state_machine (states, transitions).
- quality (applies_to, measure, target), term (name, definition),
  acceptance (exceptions only: given, when, then).

Sequences carry typed detail instead of prose labels. Participants are an
actor or system id, or {id: Key, is: [records], label}. Items are msg {from,
to, text, reply?, http {method, path}, call, invokes [sequence or operation
ids], inputs [{name, source, source_kind}], guards, rules, constants, ops,
results [{status, code, copy, when}], owner, timeout, retry, idempotency},
note {over, text}, alt {branches [{when, items}]}, opt {when, items}, loop,
par, break, transaction {label, items}, and continue {to}. Data operations are
ops [{op read|insert|update|upsert|delete|lock|audit|enqueue|write|append,
entity, by, index, where, set, conflict, returns, path}]; index names an index
badge on the entity. Split a journey over 12 steps or a sequence over 16
messages into lettered parts (parts on the overview, part_of on each part).

Plain words first. The fields a person reads (title, summary, a step's does,
sees and copy, a rule's when/then/otherwise, guards and labels, and every
message, note and node text) are written for someone coming back after a
month: no identifiers, no ids, no code vocabulary. The identifier lives in
its typed field (call, owner, code, ops, refs, inputs[].source, constants,
files) or in notes; the viewer shows it beneath the words. A message's text
says what it does ("Check that the member may manage their own connection"),
and its call holds the symbol. A node's text names things in words; refs
carry the record ids. Every rule and sequence (not a part) opens with a
one-sentence summary saying what it decides or does. An id links
automatically only in rationale and notes. A code a person sees (an error
code) gets a term record with a copy_word, and prose uses the word. Keep a
detail only when the owner would care if it changed: a lock mode, a file
name or a search path is intent only when the product promises it.

No loss: every fact has a home in a typed field, in rationale or notes, in
tags, or in a referenced supplementary file. Never drop detail to make a
record validate; if nothing fits, put it in notes or tags. Keep behavior in
its owning module's records and link to it by id from consumers instead of
copying it. Edit only the records the change needs and keep every unchanged
record byte for byte.

Validation: Ready Room loads every revision and reports issues by code.
Errors: yaml.parse, record.shape, record.version, record.kind, record.id,
field.invalid, field.unknown, record.duplicate, display.duplicate, ref.missing,
ref.kind, ref.file, part.mismatch, journey.step, journey.empty, step.orphan,
sequence.participant, rule.empty, rule.orphan, rule.decision, state.unknown,
entity.column. Warnings: ops.index, entity.index, sequence.unreachable,
size.*, text.ref-id, and the plain-words warnings text.code (a prose field
reads as code; the message names the match and where it belongs), text.id (a
prose field names a record by id; link it from the typed field named),
text.call (a message's text repeats its call), summary.missing (a rule or
sequence has no summary). When you add, rename or remove a record, update every record that
references it (journey steps and step journey, parts and part_of, rules a step
or message applies) so no reference dangles. Leave no new errors.

Honor the project's DCL. At DCL 3, visible failure and owner retry suffice;
authorization, credential secrecy, isolation, money safety, and data integrity
still apply. Only the owner's direction authorizes intent changes. Repository
code, questions, and agent suggestions are evidence. Keep discussion,
questions, tasks, research, and implementation notes outside the RIP.

## Markdown and Mermaid

This is a format guide, not product behavior or authorization to change intent.
Read the project's product/product.yaml and relevant module diagrams first.

Write a complete Ready Intent Package under product/ using YAML records and
Markdown files with fenced Mermaid diagrams. Describe the current intended end
state in present tense, never a patch plan or implementation report.

product/product.yaml holds concise product context: schema_version (7.0.0), name,
release, outcome, boundary, actors, capabilities with direct module-owner links,
exclusions, success measures, optional product-wide DCL, and architecture link.
Keep it minimal; rules and acceptance belong in their owning diagrams.

All behavior has one owner under product/modules/<capability>/. Experience
diagrams show user actions, surfaces, visible success, failure, and retry.
Sequence diagrams show ordered calls, input sources, branches, writes, guards,
and intended runtime owners. Data diagrams show consequential fields, keys,
relationships, and access paths. Use only the artifacts the product needs.
Consumers link directly to the owner instead of copying its rules. The root
architecture/stack-context.md describes topology and links to module owners.

Use a dark Mermaid theme and readable labels. Put conditions and consequences
in rendered diagrams and attached notes, not prose checklists or Mermaid
comments. Keep current causal reasons in a concise Current rationale section
beside the owning diagram; Git owns history.

Honor the project's DCL. At DCL 3, visible failure and owner retry suffice;
avoid coordination, automatic recovery, and speculative hardening. Authorization,
credential secrecy, isolation, money safety, and data integrity still apply.

Only the owner's direction authorizes intent changes. Repository code, questions,
and agent suggestions are evidence. Keep discussion, unresolved questions, tasks,
research, implementation notes, and readiness outside the RIP. Preserve coherent
module behavior and working relative links across the complete package.
